citeAs: Hoak, Blaine, and Patrick McDaniel. (2025). On Synthetic Texture Datasets: Challenges, Creation, and Curation.
creator: Blaine Hoak, Patrick McDaniel (University of Wisconsin-Madison)
description: A synthetic texture image dataset created using prompt-driven text-to-image generation and a three-stage refinement pipeline. PTD contains 246,285 images across 56 texture classes and is intended to support texture-based research such as studying texture bias, texture-object associations, and robustness.
name: Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper evaluates a sample of dataset images through a human study: 9 participants each rated 100 images on overall quality and how well the image represented the provided descriptor, using a 1-5 scale. Mean scores were compared across refinement stages, showing gradual improvements in quality and representativeness.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For human evaluation, 9 participants were each shown 100 images in random order and asked two questions for each image: overall quality and how well the image represented the provided descriptor. Ratings were given on a 1 to 5 scale, and 900 unique pre-refinement images were sampled with no duplicates between or within participant sets.
rai:dataBiases: The paper explicitly discusses bias related to texture content: PTD is designed to support measurement of texture bias in vision models and the authors analyze whether the dataset is overly biased toward certain frequencies by comparing its mean power spectrum to DTD. They report that PTD is not biased toward a certain frequency and note generation challenges such as NSFW safety filters disproportionately flagging benign texture images, especially for some texture descriptors like paisley.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected by programmatically generating images from 96,768 text prompts constructed from combinations of artistic, spatial, color-enhancer, color, and texture descriptors. These prompts were fed to Stable Diffusion, regenerating images that were flagged by the NSFW filter to maintain a consistent number of images, yielding 483,840 generated images before refinement and 246,285 after refinement.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During generation, images flagged by Stable Diffusion's NSFW filter were treated as unusable outputs: the authors regenerated flagged images to ensure a consistent number of images per prompt, and excluded flagged images from the final public dataset.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw source data consisted of synthetic images generated from text prompts using Stable Diffusion, initially totaling 483,840 images before refinement. Prompts were built from 56 texture classes and descriptor categories including artistic, spatial, enhancer, and color terms.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes several limitations: Stable Diffusion is not explicitly designed to create textures, so object-like images can arise and require filtering; structured textures such as grid and polka-dotted tend to have worse scores and leave room for improvement; NSFW safety filtering falsely flags many benign texture images; and flagged images are excluded from the released dataset.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: After generation, the dataset underwent a three-stage refinement process: frequency filtering retained the top 80% of images with the highest frequency cutoff values within each texture class to remove object-like images; patch variance filtering removed the bottom 20% of images with the lowest patch variance within each class; and CLIP score filtering removed the bottom 20% of images with the lowest CLIP scores within each texture class. Images flagged by the NSFW filter were excluded from the released dataset.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Prompts were constructed in standard English adjective order from descriptor categories. During generation, the authors analyzed NSFW-flagged outputs by temporarily disabling the filter for analysis, but excluded flagged images from release. Generated images were then processed with Fourier-based frequency analysis, non-overlapping 50x50 patch variance computation, and CLIP score computation as part of curation.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is presented as a resource for studying interpretability, model bias, security vulnerabilities, robustness, and trustworthiness in machine learning. The paper also discusses an ethical release choice: images flagged by the NSFW filter were excluded from the public release even though the authors found no explicit content in them.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended uses include texture-based research, understanding high-level features learned by models, measuring texture bias, constructing texture-object associations, studying robustness and adversarial vulnerabilities, and supporting broader texture analysis at scale.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stable Diffusion was used to generate images from prompts; its built-in NSFW safety filter was part of the filtering pipeline; and CLIP was used to score image-prompt alignment during refinement.
